reader.requirement: At --std 85 a zero divisor in any divide operation of an arithmetic statement (every DIVIDE format, a COMPUTE expression at any depth, with or without ROUNDED/REMAINDER, any divisor usage, sign or scaling) must end the arithmetic operation and raise the size error condition: with ON SIZE ERROR the resultants keep their values and the phrase runs; without it the resultants are undefined and control passes to the end of the statement (the program continues, there is no fatal condition in 1985).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal (2002): with no ON SIZE ERROR phrase and no EC-SIZE checking, 85 wraps the statement in the two-phase try and catches every raise (resultant kept, next statement runs); 2002+ lets the zero-divide escape as fatal EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE. With the phrase both editions take the same arm.

DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal: at 85 a condition whose operand reaches an arithmetic operation is wrapped in CobolSizeError.FalseWhenRaised (zero divide makes the relation FALSE); 2002+ unwrapped (fatal).

reader.edition-search: grep UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal|FalseWhenRaised|ZeroDivide|DialectLevel across src; the raise in every quotient kernel (CobolNum.Divide, CobolFloat.Div, CobolDec, CobolExact, CobolWide, CobolBig) is edition-independent.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: without ON SIZE ERROR, 85 continues with the resultant unchanged (zd1 N1-N3 printed and END reached); at --std 2023 the same program terminates 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE (fatal)'. With the phrase, identical.

reader.notes: Every quotient kernel throws CobolSizeError.ZeroDivide unconditionally; at 85 EmitArith catches it for an unphrased statement (resultant unchanged, program continues) and with the phrase runs it. Variable-length class (a) does not apply to a divisor beyond the witness run; all probed forms raise the condition. The condition-operand case (C1 FALSE) is an implementor choice outside an arithmetic statement (DOC-A.1-70 / PB5501).

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-116: rz1.cob (rz1-002) printed 'Z1 reached' and 'Z2 reached' for DIVIDE/COMPUTE by zero carrying ONLY a NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase (the phrase ignored, program continues, as the unphrased paragraph of 6.4.2 says); 'Z3 SE +0077' / 'Z4 SE +0077' for a zero divide inside FUNCTION INTEGER (B / Z) and FUNCTION MAX (1, B / Z) arguments of COMPUTE (Amendment 1 functions); 'Z5 SE +0011 +0022' REMAINDER form, quotient and remainder kept; 'Z6 SE 1 +0005 +0005' multiple GIVING receivers, one subscripted by the earlier one, all kept; 'Z7 SE +0012' / 'Z7 after' inside IF; 'Z8 SE' A / (Z * 5), 'Z9 SE' A / (Z / 1). rz2.cob (rz2-001), class c: NOT ON SIZE ERROR written before ON SIZE ERROR (the 2002+ any-order form) is refused COBOL0900 for DIVIDE and COMPUTE at 85. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.4.2  (6.4.2 The ON SIZE ERROR Phrase)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GR2' for 'Division by zero always terminates the arithmetic operation and always causes a size error condition'. No form found that escapes the size error.
